Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Good start to this game. Plenty going on. Arsenal look dangerous and capable of pinning Napoli deep into their own half, but the Italians have threatened on the break. De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Great chance from Arsenal as Eze pulls away at the back post and connects with the ball to send a header into the box. Merino connects with a diving header of his own but it’s straight at Meret and tipped over the bar.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Arsenal being patient on the edge of the box moving the ball around, but eventually it breaks down with Eze losing the ball and then fouling De Bruyne as he tries to break away.

The Napoli players feel that should have been a card.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a new leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that…

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

#1598. Tuttosport: Milan considering return attempt with Athekame with talks expected in January

AC Milan are beginning to explore the possibility of an early return for Zachary Athekame, after his start to life in France.

When they signed Athekame in the summer of 2025, Milan were aware that he was a player for the future. Nevertheless, he was still given occasional minutes last season and he could’ve been given more.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He also could’ve stayed this season; in hindsight, things are viewed differently. Yet, there would be an argument that he’d have provided some quality depth in a position of makeshift options.

According to Tuttosport this morning, via MilanPress, the Rossoneri would be keen to bring Athekame back from his loan spell in France early for several reasons. Firstly, the Swiss has reached a new level in France this season, so his return would be a permanent one.

Then, the injury issues mean that the squad is weak at full-back. So, with Ruben Amorim looking to a four-back system more frequently, he could help a lot.

It won’t be as easy as just recalling him, though. Lyon still need to be convinced and there was no agreement for his return before the summer. With this, the French club have already hinted that a fee would be required for an early return.

Talks are expected to take place in January and with Paulo Fonseca leaving the club, Athekame’s perspective on things could change. We shall have to see.

#1597. Juventus host Rennes, beaten on all four European trips to Italy, as Lepaul faces absence

Juventus return to Europa League action against a Rennes side that have lost every European away match they have played in Italy. A third win would strengthen their hold on first place after the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio left them eighth in Serie A.

Juventus need a response, and Europe offers the quickest route to one. Luciano Spalletti’s side host Franck Haise’s Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Matchday 3. They do so as leaders of the league phase. Rennes have four points.

The backdrop is uncomfortable. This is the first match since the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio that left Juventus eighth in Serie A. Spalletti watched that game from the stands while serving a one-match ban. The ban followed a confrontation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane. Assistant Marco Domenichini took charge on the bench.

Afterwards, Spalletti said he needed to take a hard look at his relationship with the players. He also admitted Juventus had been worse than Lazio. The schedule had been tight. The squad got back from Vigo at 4:30am, and it was decided they would not train that day.

The Europa League tells a different story. Juventus opened with a 5-0 home win over N.E.C. Nijmegen on 17 September. A 2-1 win at Celta followed. After that game, the coach spoke of a desire in his side not to settle.

Goals have come freely. Juventus have seven so far. The 2003/04 season is the last time the club hit the eight-goal mark across an opening trio of matches in a major European tournament. Back then, it came in the Champions League.

Randal Kolo Muani is central to that output. He has had a hand in five goals across his last five appearances in the Champions League and Europa League.

A third European win would ease some of the pressure on Spalletti. It would also tighten Juventus’ grip on top spot. The visitors will not make it easy, though. Rennes have lost only once this season.

History favours the hosts. Rennes have lost all four of their European away matches in Italy, each against a different club. Juventus were one of them. In the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final, Juventus won 4-2 on aggregate. Filippo Inzaghi scored both goals in the 2-0 win in Turin. Zinedine Zidane and Alessandro Del Piero were involved in the build-up to the second. The return leg in France ended 2-2.

Rennes’ campaign began with a goalless draw away at Sturm Graz on 16 September. They then beat OFI Crete at home on 15 October.

#1595. Conceicao starts rehab as month-long layoff remains unconfirmed

Juventus have confirmed Francisco Conceicao suffered a shoulder problem against Lazio, while local reports suggest the winger could miss around a month.

The club’s diagnosis, reported by Portuguese outlet Observador from a Juventus medical update, followed examinations after the injury on Sunday, October 18. Juventus said Conceicao had started rehabilitation, but did not give a return date.

ANSA had reported on Monday, October 19, that Conceicao was due to undergo specific tests at J Medical, with a month on the sidelines a possibility if those checks confirmed a dislocation. Observador’s account of the club update subsequently described the injury as a possible glenohumeral dislocation pending the J Medical examinations.

The distinction matters for the timetable: the roughly one-month estimate comes from local media reporting, not a recovery date announced by Juventus. Observador also reported that the club had not disclosed the expected length of his absence.

Conceicao’s injury came during the 3-0 defeat to Lazio, leaving Juventus to assess their options on the wing while he begins rehabilitation. A month-long layoff would keep the Portugal international out of selection for a significant run of fixtures, although the club has not confirmed that timeframe.

The setback puts fresh focus on the attacking contribution Juventus lose when Conceicao is unavailable. His goals and assists have been part of his contribution in Turin, and the injury adds a selection concern after a difficult result against Lazio. He has also attracted attention around his involvement at the club, as Conceicao’s role at Juventus has been discussed in recent coverage.

For now, Conceicao’s rehabilitation is under way. Juventus have yet to publish a target date for his return, while the month-long estimate remains the timeframe reported by local media.

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

Jack Grealish has been praised by fans after donating £10,000 to the fundraising campaign of an Everton supporter suffering aggressive kidney cancer.

DJ Anton Powers – an Evertonian – is believed to have shared the efforts launched by the family of Leon, 35, on Wednesday night, with Grealish quickly responding to the call-out with a generous donation.

'What an absolute gent Jack Grealish is,' Powers wrote. 'I put up an Insta story up late last night about a heartbreaking situation for a big Everton fan.

'And Jack goes on to donate to his fund. What a top guy (blue heart, hands raised emojis).'

Fans flooded the comments of Powers' missive with their own praise for the former England star, with many recalling that he has made similar impressive gestures in the past.

#1592. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

#1591. Former Chelsea star Marc Cucurella's WAG narrowly avoids being caught in Spain's deadly train crash which has killed at least 68

Published: 05:13 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 10:17 EDT, 29 October 2026

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez admitted that she was in 'shock' after revealing that she was on the train that followed Spain's deadly crash which has already claimed 68 lives.

The horrifying high-speed rail accident saw one train strike another, stationary, train on the outskirts of Toledo amid a failure to communicate about the obstruction from central command.

The country has been plunged into mourning as the death toll rises, with at least a further 100 people suffering injuries in the wake of the crash.

Many high-profile footballers in Spain and abroad have shared their sympathies in the aftermath, but Claudia Rodriguez shared hers as she revealed how close she came to travelling on the line that day.

In a story posted on Instagram, the long-time girlfriend of the Real Madrid star claimed that she had been 'on the way to Malaga on the train behind', offering all of her 'support to the victims' families and friends'.

'Guys I'm fine, my train hasn't been affected at all because there was a lot of distance from the train that has suffered the accident,' she explained in a longer post.

'We just had to turn around and go back to Madrid since it was the same route.

Marc Cucurella's partner Claudia Rodriguez revealed that she had been on the train behind the one involved in Spain's fatal crash

Their family moved to Madrid following the defender's summer transfer from Chelsea (Source: Instagram/Claudia Rodriguez)

Spain has been plunged into three days of official warning after the horrifying crash which saw a high-speed train collide with a stationary one

'I was removed from everything. To think that if it happened later it would have happened to my train but please, nothing compared to what the people who did go on that train would have happened (heart emoji) All my strength again for those families (prayer hands emoji).'

Rodriguez went on to share her support for a call to give blood in Madrid, where her family is now based following their move from Chelsea over the summer.

The Spanish Football Federation confirmed that 24 Copa del Rey matches would be postponed this week as a 'mark of respect' after the crash.

A number of LaLiga sides had been due to play on Wednesday evening, with revised dates and times for the fixtures planned by the RFEF.

'The entire Spanish football community stands united in grief over this tragedy and has made itself available to the authorities to assist the victims of this devastating accident,' a statement from the federation added.

Three days of official mourning have begun in the country just months after the year's first fatal train crash which, like the most recent, involved a collision between one high-speed Renfe train and another from rival rail operator Iryo.

More than 540 people were travelling on the two trains when the force of the crash sent two carriages skidding down a nearby slope, amplifying the damage. The crash is believed to rank as one of the most fatal in the country's history of railways.

Among the footballers to share thoughtful messages of support in a challenging time was Ballon d'Or candidate Lamine Yamal.

'My solidarity and support to all the families of the victims and those affected by the Urda disaster,' he shared. 'All support and strength to everyone.'

#1590. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 00:12, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 03:56

Everton manager David Moyes has left the door open for Jack Grealish to reignite his career at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite being punished for a disciplinary issue.

Grealish, who is currently in his second loan spell from Manchester City, was left out of the squad for Thursday's 3-1 EFL Cup win over Newcastle United due to a disciplinary breach.

Reports suggested Grealish was punished after failing to show for a training session in the lead-up to the midweek fixture.

Grealish's name was once again absent when Everton published their teamsheet for Monday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle.

Explaining the attacker's latest absence, Everton published a short statement on their official X account: "Jack Grealish is not match fit and therefore not part of tonight’s squad."

The Toffees went on to claim a 1-0 victory at St James' Park, moving them up to seventh spot in the Premier League table.

Questioned about Grealish's absence after the win, Moyes told BBC Sport: "He's unavailable at the moment, and we will make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back."

When asked whether his omission was fitness-related, the Everton boss said: "All I'm giving out is that he is unavailable at the moment."

In his post-match press conference, Moyes admitted he was unsure whether Grealish would be back in the squad for Friday's home clash against Coventry City.

However, he was able to offer a clearer response when asked if there is a chance for the 31-year-old to return, telling reporters: “Of course there is, yes."

The upcoming meeting against Frank Lampard's side represents Everton's final game before the international break.

There is perhaps some sense in Everton keeping Grealish on the sidelines before bringing him back into the fold for the first game after the international window against Brentford.

That would give the club time to allow the situation to cool and offer Grealish time to try to earn some trust back in training over the two-week break.

#1587. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

ChelseaAug 24: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3Aug 27: Chelsea 2 Luton Town 0 (Carabao Cup)Aug 30: Chelsea 4 Brighton 3Sep 6: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1586. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

#1585. Liverpool predicted lineup vs. Fenerbahce: Andoni Iraola faces midfield choice after Dominik Szoboszlai returns from injury

By Anthony Nolan | 03 Nov 2026 00:28

Liverpool will travel to take on Turkish giants Fenerbahce on Wednesday, battling to keep their perfect start to the Champions League's league-phase intact.

Andoni Iraola's Reds were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal on Sunday afternoon, though the boss will be pleased with his team's performance overall - as well as the fact there were no new injuries from the intense showdown at Anfield.

With that in mind, Alisson Becker should start in goal this week, shielded by captain Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet at centre-back, while youngster Giovanni Leoni is closing in on a return to training after more than a year out due to an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Flanking the centre-halves will be Ronald Araujo at right-back and Kostas Tsimikas on the left, with the Greek star likely to come into the XI in place of the rested Milos Kerkez, and both Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring) and Conor Bradley (knee) unavailable.

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal, though he looks set for a start at the base of midfield alongside Alexis Mac Allister, who is expected to be substituted for either Trey Nyoni or Dominik Szoboszlai in the second half.

In the attacking third, Rio Ngumoha should start on the right wing, with Bradley Barcola on the left, the latter looking for his first goals since netting a hat-trick during the 6-3 win over LASK on matchday two.

Alexander Isak could begin the night on the bench, presenting an opportunity for Lewis Koumas to lead the line, supported by Florian Wirtz from the number 10 role while striker Hugo Ekitike continues his rehabilitation following the Achilles rupture he suffered in April.

Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Koumas

#1584. Derry City TEAR UP James McClean's contract: Poppy protest footballer's nightmare return to childhood club comes to an end amid claims he was 'permanently incapacitated'

Published: 10:35 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 10:26 EDT, 29 October 2026

The ugly dispute between James McClean and Derry City is finally over after his contract was torn up.

Earlier this month, McClean, 37, branded it 'incomprehensible' and a 'dangerous precedent' for the club to try and terminate his deal due to his physical issues when they claimed he was 'permanently incapacitated'.

But the Republic of Ireland international, who refused to wear a poppy on Remembrance weekend while representing English and Welsh clubs at the height of his career, has now come to an agreement with his boyhood side. He had two years left on the deal.

It is a nightmare end to what was supposed to be a fairytale homecoming having signed in January and McClean had not been included in a matchday squad since July as the relationship soured.

'I am pleased that we have reached a resolution to settle these matters, his statement read. 'While my return to the Club did not work out as I had hoped, Derry City FC will always hold a special place in my heart.

'I want to thank the fans for their support, and I wish the squad, the management, staff, and the supporters the very best for the future. In particular, I want to wish the team the best of luck in the FAI Cup Final against Waterford FC.'

James McClean's return to Derry City is over after his contract was torn up

Derry City chairman Philip O’Doherty thanked McClean for his 'dedication'.

'His achievements extend far beyond the Brandywell; amassing 103 senior caps for the Republic of Ireland is a remarkable milestone, and we want to formally acknowledge his immense contribution to Irish football as a whole,' he said.

'We wish him the very best for the future. Neither the club nor James McClean will be making any further comment on this matter.'

Derry attempted to axe McClean in August – despite signing him in January on a multi-year deal – reportedly claiming he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

The former Wrexham man insisted he was ready to feature when called upon in a defiant statement.

'This has been one of the most difficult periods of my life, both personally and professionally,' McClean said in a statement on the PFA Ireland website on October 6.

'When I agreed to come home from Wrexham, I did so in good faith, based on commitments made to me both playing wise and regarding my future after football. I uprooted my family midway through the school year because I believed in the vision presented to me, both for the short term and the long term.

'I accept that some of my actions over the past few months were misjudged, and my frustrations should have remained in-house. I take responsibility for that - and I apologise. Derry City is my club, and I respect everyone who cares about it as much as I do.

'I was asked to help drive standards, to speak up, and to use my experience to further professionalise my hometown club. From the start of the season, I tried to do this to the best of my ability, but I felt when I did my opinions were not well received.

McLean is pictured alongside Adam O'Reilly before Derry City's UEFA Conference League game against HNK Rijeka back in July

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

'While I'm happy to hold myself accountable when I am wrong and when my performances have not been to the levels I expect of myself, I cannot understand or accept that I have been treated this way over the past few months.

'For any club to feel it is OK to attempt to terminate a player's contract without any due process or just cause is incomprehensible, and it sets a dangerous precedent for every player in this league.'

But now that fractious relationship is over, with a mutual agreement over the contract termination reached.

McClean is most famous on these shores for his refusal to take part in wearing a poppy and has previously spoken out about his reasons for not doing so, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012.

He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

The winger grew up on the Creggan estate in Londonderry, an area that was directly affected by the Bloody Sunday massacre in 1972 when British soldiers shot 26 unarmed civilians during a protest march, with 14 killed.

A quote in the 37-year-old's biography The Walls sheds light on his thinking, speaking about the IRA.

It reads: 'I’m not claiming that every action was justified. Obviously, I don’t support anyone innocent being killed. But I am saying that I supported the original end goal, even if that involved bloodshed '

After being asked about those comments in this interview, McClean added: 'When you grow up listening to the stories there’s a part of you thinking: "These are heroes. I wish I was part of that or born a decade earlier". I’d be a hypocrite if I sat here and said I didn’t support their cause.

'Don’t get me wrong; I don’t believe that anybody innocent deserved to be killed, right? Unfortunately, it was a dirty war, and there were a lot of casualties on both sides.'

McClean pictured in action for West Brom against Huddersfield in 2017 not wearing the poppy

He also spoke at length about his decision not to wear the poppy two years ago: 'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well as many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean explained in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour World War 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both World Wars.

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he has received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy", and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'
