#1582. Douglas Luiz finally opens his Juventus account as Spalletti hails display at Lecce

Douglas Luiz has finally scored for Juventus. The Brazilian midfielder found the net in Sunday’s 2-0 win at Lecce, more than two years after his €50m move from Aston Villa, and he also set up the opening goal for Weston McKennie.

It was a night that changed the conversation around a player who has spent much of his time in Turin under scrutiny. Luciano Spalletti was quick to single him out afterwards, and the club’s own numbers show just how rare an evening like this has been for him.

According to the standout stats published by Juventus on Monday, this was the first time Douglas Luiz had both scored and assisted in the same match in Europe’s top five leagues. Before Sunday he had made 261 appearances in those competitions without managing it.

The club also points out that he now has two goal involvements from eight Serie A appearances this season, one goal and one assist. In the 2024/25 campaign he played 19 league games for Juventus and failed to register either.

Both contributions came before the break. His free kick was dinked over the Lecce defence for McKennie to break the offside line and slide in on 29 minutes. Twelve minutes later, Federico Gatti laid the ball off and Douglas Luiz hit it first time from outside the box into the far corner.

Douglas Luiz’s first goal in Bianconero! ⚪⚫ pic.twitter.com/g2vTIhUEnF

JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 25, 2026

The midfielder did not dwell on the personal milestone. In comments shared by the club’s press room after the game, he put the result first.

“The most important thing today was to win. I’m really happy with the result because we’ve worked so hard, and I’m delighted for the team. This victory also gives us the confidence we need,” he said.

He was also honest about the second half, when Lecce pushed Juventus back. “We played well in the first half, but I think we could definitely have done better in the second. We need to improve and perform well for the full 90 minutes.”

Speaking to DAZN, he added that the set piece routine involving Teun Koopmeiners is something the squad practises a lot, and that the players were pleased for their coach after a difficult week, as Tuttosport reported.

Spalletti had already explained after the 3-0 defeat by Lazio that he wanted changes, as covered in our piece on the changes Spalletti identified. Since then Juventus have moved to a three-man midfield, and Douglas Luiz has been one of the beneficiaries.

Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the coach was full of praise for the Brazilian. “He had a great game today, he fought and ran, he battled on all sides and he helped clean up certain situations when we needed him to,” Spalletti said, in quotes reported by Football Italia.

He came off after 82 minutes, replaced by Sarr, having done the bulk of the work in a side that had only 17 outfield players available. With Manuel Locatelli and Khéphren Thuram among the absentees listed in our latest injury update, Spalletti needs exactly this kind of reliability from his remaining midfielders.

One good night does not settle a debate that has followed Douglas Luiz since his arrival. What it does give him is a platform. If he can keep producing this level of energy and quality in a system that suits him, the midfielder who struggled to make an impact in his first season may yet become an important figure for Spalletti this term.

Sources: Juventus FC, Football Italia, Tuttosport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1581. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'set sights' on Junior Kroupi swoop - but face competition from two Champions League clubs

By Ben Sully | 03 Nov 2026 01:05, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 02:50

Arsenal have reportedly earmarked Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi as a transfer target ahead of the January window.

The Gunners currently enjoy a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League table after winning eight of their nine matches this season.

Arsenal's league position is largely based on a strong backline that has recorded six clean sheets, the latest of which came in Sunday's hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool.

While their backline is their major strength, Arsenal can still improve at the opposite end of the pitch, which is an area Mikel Arteta is keen to address in the winter transfer window.

According to The Mirror, the Arsenal boss has made signing a 'top-class' striker his main priority for the winter market.

Arteta can currently call upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as his main centre-forward options, but the latter has netted just once in 12 appearances this term and has been linked with a potential move away.

The report claims the Gunners have their sights on Bournemouth's Kroupi, although they will need to overcome some major obstacles to pull off the transfer in the new year.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and German giants Bayern Munich are among those obstacles, with the European heavyweights believed to be among Kroupi's suitors.

Even if they can get ahead of their competition, Arsenal would still face the difficult task of convincing Bournemouth to part ways with an important player in the middle of the season.

Kroupi finished the 2025-26 Premier League season as Bournemouth's top scorer after netting 13 goals in 33 appearances.

The Frenchman's progress has been hampered by a foot injury which required surgery and forced him to miss the first two months of the season.

Kroupi has recently returned to the fray with three substitute appearances, although Bournemouth boss Marco Rose is keen to exercise caution with the minutes he gives the 20-year-old as he continues to build up fitness.

With Kroupi being eased back into action, Bournemouth will be reluctant to sanction his departure in January, especially as they will want to keep their key players to give them the best chance of enjoying success this term.

The Cherries harbour ambitions of going a long way in the Europa League, while they are also looking to match or go close to equalling last season's sixth-place finish in the Premier League.

#1580. 'It's a travesty and not what they were promised': Glazers' anger at Sir Jim Ratcliffe's reign revealed - and why Man United have become debt-loaded inconvenience for absentee landlords as they splash cash on true loves

Published: 13:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EDT, 29 October 2026

From a safe distance in Florida, out of the line of fire, the Glazer family are happy for others to let it be known they are disenchanted with how they believe the British businessman who paid them £1.5billion for a minority share in Manchester United has mismanaged the club.

‘It’s a travesty and not what they expected or were promised,’ a source with a social connection to the family tells Daily Mail Sport of Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s disastrous custodianship. ‘They have never run the club this way.’

Another source told the US broadcaster ESPN this week that the Glazers believe Ratcliffe ‘couldn't have masterminded a worse situation’. His ‘downgrading in all departments’ at Old Trafford was ‘the opposite of what he said his strategy is’.

It would be unwise to characterise this Glazer concern as sentiment. Cash is the motivating factor, just as always. United are two points off the bottom of the Premier League ahead of Saturday’s trip to Chelsea and the $6bn (£4.5bn) valuation which the Glazers put on the club when seeking a buyer, four years ago, is looking more unrealistic than ever.

The Glazers control any sale. A clause in their deal with Ratcliffe, completed in 2024, lets them force him out of his 28 per cent stake – and out of the entire landscape – if they sell the club to a third party, without him having any say, unless he can match that offer and buy the entire club himself. Which is highly improbable.

Whatever displeasure they might feel, they can’t buy back Ratcliffe’s piece of the United pie. But from next February, Ratcliffe will be powerless to stop them selling the entire club for a price lower than the $33 (£25) a share he paid for his chunk. As of Thursday, the United share price was just $20.77 (£15.60).

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (right) with Man United co-chairman Avram Glazer, who is rarely seen at Old Trafford and has never given a meaningful interview about the club he owns

United fans make clear their disgust at the way the club is being run by the Glazers and Ineos

Ratcliffe’s Ineos are cutting their losses in football. They put their Swiss club FC Lausanne-Sport up for sale this week and have slashed the asking price for their French club Nice.

They could sell their chunk of United to someone else if at least two of Ineos’ three shareholders – Ratcliffe and company co-founders Andrew Currie and John Reece – agree to it. The Glazers, for their part, may want to see United’s new stadium built, hiking up the value, before selling. That might not be completed until 2035.

More than ever, the Glazers are absentee landlords. A family with far bigger fish to fry than their struggling Premier League asset where fans sing against them. A family who have been extremely active elsewhere while Old Trafford burns.

In February, Avram Glazer, one of the six siblings, bid $1.32bn (£1bn) for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru franchise in cricket's Indian Premier League, where the enormous market and broadcasting rights deals have seen stratospheric returns on investment. Only as the franchise’s valuation approached a prohibitive $2bn (£1.5bn) did Glazer withdraw. His bid for the Rajasthan Royals was also retracted.

And then there is the love of the Glazers’ lives – their Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFL franchise – where their active involvement provides a striking contrast to their loveless 21-year ownership of United.

While the family have managed to go all these years without a single meaningful UK media interview about United – Avram Glazer hastily climbed into his Aston Martin and drove off when doorstepped by a Sky TV reporter in Florida, five years ago – a recent Amazon series about the Buccaneers provided a rare glimpse into the world of these billionaires.

Like so many such series, Raise the Flags is sanitised and glossy, with Ed Glazer, another of the siblings, one of its executive producers. But it paints a revealing picture of how the NFL-mad Glazers tried and failed for years to buy into the sport, which was intrinsic to the siblings’ childhoods, until the death of Bucs owner Hugh Culverhouse finally gave Malcolm Glazer, their father, his chance in 1995.

They were seen as saviours at a franchise which was ridiculed for always losing and at risk of relocation to Baltimore, Maryland, 1,000 miles away. They transformed it, appointing rookie coach Tony Dungy and even changing the colours from garish neon orange to red and pewter grey.

Joel Glazer, who last visited Old Trafford in 2019, becomes emotional as he tells filmmakers about the team’s legendary win under Dungy, against the San Francisco 49ers in 1997, which set them on the way from hapless also-rans to two-time Super Bowl winners.

Manchester United co-owner Joel Glazer celebrates Super Bowl glory in 2021 when his beloved Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Kansas City Chiefs

The Bucs, not United, is what gets the Glazers out of bed. It’s what they spend their own money on – and that will include a $1bn (£750m) rebuild of the team’s Raymond James stadium

‘You know, you felt we’d turned the corner,’ he says, his voice breaking. There is an authenticity about this.

The Bucs, not Manchester United, is what gets these brothers out of bed in the morning. It’s what they spend their own money on – and that will include a $1bn (£750m) rebuild of the team’s Raymond James stadium – the ‘RayJay’ – which is old, dated and lacks the roof required for Tampa to host a lucrative Super Bowl. Within two months, the Glazers and the Bucs will outline plans for the overhaul, to conform with a deadline for a lease extension on the ground.

United have their own stadium plans, of course. But the Glazers didn’t even attend the event at Old Trafford in March 2025, at which architect Sir Norman Foster’s proposals, with their distinctive, canopy-like roof, were presented.

While United are a globally recognised brand and the Bucs are a franchise little known beyond the US, there is no doubt which of these two Glazer sports businesses holds most financial value.

The wild expectation that United would fetch $6bn was born of the values of NFL franchises such as Washington Commanders, on the market for $8bn (£6bn) at the time they put United up for sale. The Commanders were eventually sold for $6.05bn (£4.45bn) to a consortium led by Josh Harris, who also has a big chunk of Crystal Palace. There was no offer anywhere in that vicinity for United.

In part, NFL teams have become so valuable because of a US tax break which allows owners to claim tax deductions on things their teams own or pay for and shrink the amount of profit they pay tax on. It means billionaire owners like the Glazers can end up paying a lower percentage of their income in tax than the workers who keep the stadium running.

In the NFL, the Seattle Seahawks were sold in early September for $9.6bn (£7.2bn), a world record for a sports franchise that lasted just a few days until basketball’s LA Lakers changed hands for $12.5bn (£9.3bn) – more than double United’s industry valuation.

With a precious NFL asset to protect and build, United, whose football operations have been ceded to Ratcliffe, are a minor consideration.

Joel and Avram Glazer are often seen in and around the Bucs - but are rarely spotted at Old Trafford

Former Bucs head coach Tony Dungy was once under pressure like Michael Carrick is now but the Glazers stood by their man - and felt the benefits

Though the Amazon series is PR-friendly and soft focus, it offers an intriguing insight into what active Glazer involvement can look like. When the first draft under their ownership takes place, some of the brothers are in the Buccaneers ‘War Room’ witnessing the squad being built.

When Coach Dungy struggles with no wins in five in his second season and faces a critique like the one Michael Carrick is now encountering, the Glazers call him in for lunch. Rather than tell him he is fired – as he expects – they talk things over for four hours and put him at ease. Dungy’s testimony corroborates the notion that they helped him.

Joel Glazer was often seen as a meddling man of interference at United, prior to Ratcliffe moving in. He would ask for higher fees and drive harder deals when executive chairman Ed Woodward or others were trying to negotiate.

The family never wanted an Amazon documentary about United and only now, under Ratcliffe, has the streaming business got into the corridors of the club. The Glazers’ key United manoeuvres, still very much going on, take place behind closed doors.

The evidence of the past year points to them continuing to use the club as collateral to secure huge loans which helps them invest in other parts of their business empire, according to a study by the respected football finance expert Paul Quinn, popularly known as ‘The Esk’.

Quinn highlights a UK Companies House filing from February, ‘Charge 0018’, through which United took out a Bank of America mortgage against land near Old Trafford, and other club assets, to potentially generate cash for the Glazers. The loan arrangement, taking United’s maximum credit facility up to £400m, came a few weeks before Avram Glazer submitted his huge bids for an IPL franchise.

There is no evidence that the new borrowing secured by Charge 0018 funded an IPL bid, or that Manchester United’s money was used to finance one.

More than ever, it is the Glazers’ own elusive cash that the club need. That new £2billion stadium won’t build itself and though there are plenty of ways of finding the money, the Financial Times has pointed out while listing them that they will ‘not come cheap’.

More than ever, it is the Glazers’ own elusive cash that Manchester United need. That new £2billion stadium won’t build itself

Carrick will be fighting for his future when his United team take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday

Tapping into the bond market as Barcelona did to finance their $1.5bn upgrade of Camp Nou would leave the club more exposed to global interest rates. Private equity funds would want a major pay-back when the stadium is built, limiting United’s capacity to earn from the new structure.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play Atlanta Falcons at the RayJay on Sunday and there can be no doubt that some of the Glazer brothers will be there. Bryan, Joel and Avram were in the team locker room after last weekend’s win at the Carolina Panthers, by all accounts smiling and clapping as coach Todd Bowles spoke.

They hardly ever watch United these days and will certainly not be at Stamford Bridge to see Carrick fighting for his future. Their Premier League asset is an inconvenience, loaded down with debt payments, running up losses for the past seven years and, on Ratcliffe’s watch, reduced to selling clumps of Old Trafford turf for £125.

Where are the Glazers? More than 4,000 miles away from all that.

#1579. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: ‘We have no fear at all’, Pau Torres identifies Barca weakness

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 06:55, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Barcelona have been through a run of tricky games, losing their 100% record in the Champions League and La Liga to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and now, after recovering with two wins, they face another big challenge. On Tuesday, Barcelona host Aston Villa at the Camp Nou.

The English side have won every game in the European competition and are unbeaten in five Premier League matches. That is why Pau Torres, an undisputed starter for Aston Villa, is not afraid at all of the game against Barcelona.

‘We have no fear at all, but we do have respect. We know how difficult it will be, but nothing is impossible. We will try to compete with our own weapons’ - he said in an interview with Catalan newspaper Sport.

The 29-year-old defender also pointed out what to exploit in the contest.

Barcelona, under the management of Hansi Flick, are characterised by heavy pressing in the attacking half, which forces a high defensive line to keep up with the rest of the team. That space is something for Aston Villa to exploit, as Pau Torres explained, based on the profile of their trio of very quick attackers, including a Brazilian.

‘This year we have very vertical players, such as Ibrahim Mbaye, Alysson and Nicolas Jackson himself. They work very well when opponents leave space behind the defence.’

Of course, there is a way to attack, but for more than 60% of the time Barcelona’s opponents will be defending. Focus is a must if they are to avoid conceding against Barcelona, who have scored 57 times in 14 matches this season. ‘If we want to get a positive result, we will have to be alert defensively.’

Pau Torres also has a special mission. As a left-sided centre-back, he could come up against right winger Lamine Yamal several times because of the cover he will have to provide for left-back Ian Maatsen, who is known for being very attacking.

‘When you play this type of match, you always want to face the best to find out what level you are at. It will be a pleasure to play against Lamine and have to mark him on some occasions.

He always surprises, he is unpredictable and, often, just one player to mark him is not enough. We will have to be very alert to the cover from team-mates.’

The clash, which promises to be an interesting one, kicks off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday. Aston Villa share top spot in the Champions League league phase with Paris Saint-Germain, who are ahead on goals scored, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis. Barcelona are looking to recover after losing 4-2 to leaders Paris Saint-Germain in the last round.

#1578. Allegri banned for Juventus reunion as Napoli lodge appeal

Massimiliano Allegri will not be on the Napoli bench when his side visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Serie A’s sporting judge has suspended the former Juventus coach for two matches following his dismissal against Roma, although Napoli have confirmed they will challenge the decision.

The ban means one of the most talked about reunions of the autumn could take place without its main character in the dugout, unless the appeal goes Napoli’s way before the weekend.

Allegri was sent off late in Saturday’s 3-3 draw with Roma at the Maradona, reacting furiously after Leonardo Balerdi struck a late equaliser for the visitors. As Football Italia reported, he removed his jacket and walked away before returning and having to be held back by his own staff.

The judge’s ruling, published on Monday and detailed by Sky Sport Italia, goes further than the touchline incident. Allegri was punished for an insulting remark aimed at the match officials in the 90th minute, a seriously disrespectful comment directed at them in the dressing room area afterwards, and aggressive behaviour towards an executive of the opposing club. The first two were noted by the fourth official and the referee, the last by staff working for the federal prosecutor.

On top of the suspension, the 59-year-old has been fined €10,000.

The two games Allegri is set to miss are both away from home. Napoli travel to Monza in the midweek round on Wednesday 28 October, before heading to Turin to face Juventus on Sunday 1 November, with both matches kicking off at 20:45 local time.

If the ban stands, his first game back on the bench would be the home fixture against Lazio on Sunday 8 November.

Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) October 26, 2026

Napoli moved quickly. In a short club statement on Monday afternoon, the Partenopei said that, having requested access to the official documents, they would lodge an appeal against the two match suspension handed to their coach.

Sky Sport Italia notes that a successful appeal would open the door for Allegri to take his place on the bench in Turin. Italian reports suggest the case should be heard before the end of the week, so the picture ought to be clear before Sunday.

For Juventus supporters, any meeting with Allegri carries extra weight. He led the club across two spells, the second of which ended in May 2024, and he remains one of the most successful coaches in its history.

Luciano Spalletti’s side head into the week in a better mood after ending a 35 day wait for a league win with the 2-0 victory at Lecce, which lifted them to seventh on 14 points. Douglas Luiz was among the scorers that night, as covered in our report on his first goal for the club.

Whether or not Allegri is in the dugout, Napoli will arrive as a dangerous opponent. You can follow every twist in his relationship with the Bianconeri on our Massimiliano Allegri page.

#1577. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Possession: Manchester United 59%-41% SabahShots: 14-4Shots on target: 5-0Corners: 6-2Touches in opposition box: 35-4

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1576. Official: Baresi honoured by City of Milano with inscription in the Famedio

Franco Baresi’s passing has left a hole in the hearts of AC Milan fans, but also of those in the city of Milano.

Some footballers transcend the game, especially those who become something else. For Baresi, football allowed him to offer more to the city that raised him through his extensive charity work. However, it wasn’t just the citizens of Milano who benefited from this.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Through the Fondazione Milan, the former defender helped people across the globe and that is why he’s considered so highly.

He was an excellent defender, perhaps an even better servant to the Rossoneri, but he was above all, he was a fantastic man. It speaks volumes that tributes still arrive for him and that the city stood still on the day of his service.

Baresi has already been remembered with murals, but the City of Milan have now offered their own memorial to one of its greatest sons, as the club detailed in a statement this afternoon.

“The City of Milano today honoured Franco Baresi, AC Milan’s legendary Captain, by inscribing his name in the Famedio at the Monumental Cemetery, a memorial dedicated to the figures who have shaped the city’s history and identity.

“The ceremony, led by Mayor Giuseppe Sala and City Council President Elena Buscemi, took place in the presence of Franco Baresi’s family and AC Milan Legend and Brand Ambassador Daniele Massaro, representing the Club.

“Baresi was honoured alongside 13 other distinguished figures, recognising both his extraordinary achievements on the pitch and the values he represented to generations of supporters and the wider Milan community.

“Born in Travagliato, near Brescia, Franco Baresi devoted his life to AC Milan and the city of Milano from a young age. He played a defining role in one of the greatest eras in football history. The Club retired his number 6 shirt in his honour and celebrated his 50 years with AC Milan in 2024. He had served as Honorary Vice President since 2020.

“Others honoured this year include Ornella Vanoni, a devoted Rossoneri supporter, Bruno Pizzul, Giovanni Gastel and Don Antonio Mazzi, alongside prominent figures from Milano’s cultural and civic life.

“Since December 2024, as part of the Club’s 125th anniversary celebrations, the Famedio’s Crypt has also been the final resting place of AC Milan founder Herbert Kilpin, alongside other figures who have shaped the city’s history, including Giuseppe Meazza, Giorgio Gaber, Enzo Jannacci and Alda Merini.

“The tribute to Franco Baresi goes far beyond football. It reflects the deep bond between AC Milan and Milano, a city whose history, social fabric and cultural identity the Club has helped shape for more than 125 years.”

#1575. Spalletti open to 3-4-2-1 at Genoa but expects few changes with Napoli next

Luciano Spalletti is ready to shift from a 3-5-2 to a 3-4-2-1 at Genoa, with Alajbegovic among the options behind the striker. With eight players injured and Napoli due on Sunday, he expects his team to stay broadly the same.

Luciano Spalletti is ready to tweak his shape at Genoa without tearing up his team. On the eve of the trip, the Juventus coach said one very small positional change turns the 3-5-2 into a 3-4-2-1. Anyone, he added, can fill the two roles behind the striker.

He named Alajbegovic, Boga and Zhegrova as options in that zone. Kolo Muani was his example of the profile he has in mind. Spalletti said the forward can play partly as a number 10 and partly as a wide forward. Sarr has recovered and is available.

Tuttosport expects Alajbegovic to possibly replace Kolo Muani behind Woltemade, and sees Cambiaso as the only left-flank option with Celik injured.

The fixture list explains the caution. The trip to Genoa is the first of two games in five days. Spalletti is weighing a few rotations partly because of the second of those games, Sky Sport reported. Asked about Napoli, the coach said everything has to be taken into account. He still expects the team to stay broadly the same.

Spalletti also said his players are fully focused and have the right mentality. That follows a mixed run. Juventus lost at home to Lazio on 18 October. Afterwards Spalletti said his side had shown fragility that starts in the mind. He added that tactical systems change nothing without hunger, passion, courage and character. A draw with Rennes followed.

The win at Lecce began to make up for both results. McKennie volleyed in a Douglas Luiz free kick in the 29th minute. Douglas Luiz added the second four minutes before half-time.

Spalletti described Genoa as an extremely hard opponent, citing both the atmosphere at their ground and their tactics. He warned they can use their physical strength at set pieces and also run in behind defences. Above all, he said, the side carries Daniele De Rossi’s fighting spirit.

The warning on dead balls fits recent meetings between the clubs. Six of the last ten goals between the clubs came from set pieces: two from corners, one from a throw-in and three from penalties.

🗣️ "We must put in convincing performances"

Luciano Spalletti looks ahead to #GenoaJuve in his pre-match press conference ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/r2x4ICLz15 pic.twitter.com/tWcJLMx0Ia

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 27, 2026

History still favours Juventus. They have lost only one of their last 12 Serie A games against Genoa, with nine wins and two draws. They have also won the last four. That lone defeat was 2-1 at the Ferraris on 6 May 2022. Juventus have scored 233 goals against Genoa, more than any other club in the league.

After Genoa, Juventus host Massimiliano Allegri’s Napoli in Serie A Matchday 10 on Sunday 1 November, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1573. Liverpool Confidential: Inside Harvey Elliott's difficult start to life in Valencia, why experts think move is doomed despite efforts off the pitch, the loanee who IS thriving in Spain and club's stance on making Ronald Araujo deal permanent

Published: 13:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 13:05 EDT, 29 October 2026

Harvey Elliott is working hard to right the wrongs of his first few months at Valencia as another loan away from Liverpool threatens to become a 'significant disappointment' due to concerns over his form, fitness and discipline.

The English midfielder is on loan at the Estadio Mestalla after a rotten year at Aston Villa but he has struggled for game time under two different managers, making just six substitute appearances so far.

And last weekend he suffered the ignominy of being sent off just 19 minutes after coming off the bench at home to Villarreal, who then scored a 90th-minute winner seconds later to leave Valencia second-bottom after 10 games.

Liverpool staff are in constant contact with all their loanees and their clubs to check on players' progress and the last word back from Valencia was that Elliott, 23, is putting in quality work off the pitch to improve physically.

But as Julian Burgos, a Valencia expert, tells Liverpool Confidential: ‘At the moment, I don’t think he has adapted… he has been a significant disappointment, especially considering he arrived with the pedigree of coming from Liverpool.

‘It is true that he has been putting in the work over the last few weeks, and he appears to be in better physical shape.

Harvey Elliott is on loan at Valencia but 'has been a significant disappointment' says Julian Burgos, a Valencia expert

Elliott was sent off against Villarreal at the weekend despite coming on as a substitute

‘Honestly, if the option to terminate the loan arises, Valencia will likely pursue it. With a new sporting director and manager – compounded by the team’s poor form – it seems they will look to undo many of the moves made by the previous sporting director, the Scotsman Ron Gourlay.'

Valencia sacked their previous coach, Carlos Corberan, in mid-September after they picked up just one point in their opening five matches of the season.

‘They need to free up space within the salary cap to make changes to the squad,' Burgos adds, 'so they will likely take any opportunity to cut ties with players brought in under the previous regime.’

Last year, the midfielder was stuck at Aston Villa. Clearly not fancied by their manager Unai Emery, the club prevented him from playing the 10 games that would have meant the deal becoming permanent for £35million, which seemed a foregone conclusion when he joined.

As Elliott featured for Liverpool at the start of last season – a five-minute cameo off the bench in their second game of the campaign – he could not head out on another loan because of a FIFA ruling that states players can only represent two clubs on the pitch in one season.

There is no option or obligation to make his deal permanent at Valencia, whose new manager is Javier Aguirre, whom England fans may remember for his touchline antics with Mexico at the World Cup. Aguirre will give Elliott time to turn his fortunes around. There is an understanding he needed to build fitness after barely playing last year.

The club have appealed last week's red card – for two yellows – and Elliott is said to have apologised to team-mates.

Elliott had a miserable time at Aston Villa last season when he hardly featured for the club

…but it’s not all worrying news in Valencia!

Now let’s head across the city to fellow La Liga club Levante, where one Liverpool loanee is thriving.

Centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe has been touted as having the potential to be ‘one of the best in the world in his position’.

Burgos adds: ‘Since his debut against Sevilla four matches ago, he has established himself as a starter for the manager Luis Castro, who asserted that he possesses the qualities to become one of the best players in the world in his position.

‘Against Sevilla, he recovered from an early mistake to score the equalising goal in stoppage time, and he has been a fixture in the side ever since. At 18, he has an impressive physique, remarkable coordination for his height, and the makings of a great footballer – both for the present and, even more so, for the future.’

Ndukwe could not stay at Liverpool this season due to a work permit issue. Apparently he now has the required points to return to Anfield and a recall clause is included in the deal.

But it might be better to keep Ndukwe there, where he is playing every week, and bleed him into the first-team squad next year.

Liverpool centre back Ifeanyi Ndukwe has shone at Levante this season and is now a regular starter for his manager Luis Castro

Ndukwe could not stay at Liverpool this season due to a work permit issue. He now has the required points to return to Anfield

The story of the week at Liverpool has been Ronald Araujo after his man-of-the-match performance against Brighton. The Uruguayan’s status as a cult hero continues to grow and grow.

But are fans naive to fall in love with a loan player? Will Liverpool make the temporary move permanent? And can they do it for less than the clause of £47m?

Last week, I said I’d answer fans’ questions every week in this column and the answers to the Araujo inquiries are…

Absolutely, fans are right to fall in love with him! Liverpool are open to making the move permanent if this form continues, for sure – otherwise why would they insert the option to do so in the deal? People may point to the fact Liverpool would not usually sign a 28-year-old (Araujo turns 28 in March) but look at Virgil van Dijk, still going strong at 35.

And yes, they will be able to negotiate the fee down from the pre-agreed figure with Barcelona.

Ronald Araujo has been sensational for his manager Andoni Iraola this season

Lots of talk about Trent Alexander-Arnold this week given he has fallen out of favour with new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho. It has led many to debate whether Liverpool should re-sign him but Confidential is told Alexander-Arnold remains happy in the Spanish capital.

Regardless, would it be a wise move? Financially, no. Does the team lack his creativity from right back? Yes. Would the fans welcome him back with open arms? No… but stranger things have happened.

Trent Alexander-Arnold has fallen out of favour at Real - but a return to Anfield looks unlikely

Fans of French club Lens have been banned from buying tickets for their team’s Champions League trip to Anfield.

Lens, who finished second in Ligue 1 last year under now Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage, come to Liverpool in the new year. But they will do so – as it stands – without supporters after UEFA banned them from selling away tickets following events in Belgium last week.

In Lens' loss at Bruges, fans were punished for lighting and throwing pyrotechnics – which injured disabled supporters.

The club banned its own fans from buying tickets for this week’s trip to rivals Lille and said in a statement: ‘This situation goes far beyond the realm of the displays that sometimes accompany popular expression in the stands. A red line has been crossed. This line was not implicit.’

Anfield also had an empty away end last year when Galatasaray came to town in the last 16, a match which the Reds won 4-0.

Big Mama’s best night… no thanks to dud water bottle

An important night for Giorgi Mamardashvili against Chelsea on Wednesday.

The big Georgian has had mixed reviews since his arrival from Valencia, with some indifferent performances.

But this was perhaps his best performance yet – not just for his fine penalty save, but some other notable stops as both he and Mike Penders kept the scores level.

Liverpool’s No 2 can poke fun, though, at whoever provided the notes for his water bottle ahead of the shootout. None of the instructions were correct and Mamardashvili was left diving the wrong way several times.

Giorgi Mamardashvili celebrates his side's victory over Chelsea with his team-mate Kostas Tsimikas. It was the goalkeeper's finest performance in a Liverpool shirt

Sunday’s clash with Arsenal is the biggest game so far in the Andoni Iraola era for one reason: it sets the tone for the rest of the season. Lose and Liverpool are nine points behind the champions. Win, though, and it’s only three – with confidence they can beat anyone.

Dominik Szoboszlai is pushing to return but here is a question for you to ponder to finish this week’s column: does last year’s player of the year get back in Iraola’s best XI?
